title: Validate every change as testaccount before CASE switchover
context: Nix is not yet installed on AVA. The first real darwin-rebuild switch is a high-risk event because CASE owns the daily-driver session, the 1Password SSH agent socket, and live ~/dotfiles symlinks. testaccount already exists with /bin/zsh and is otherwise untouched, making it a clean substrate for iterative validation.
decision: All darwin-rebuild switches run as testaccount on AVA first. CASE migrates in-place via home-manager.backupFileExtension="hm-backup" only after the configuration has demonstrated parity under testaccount. testaccount persists indefinitely as the validation user — every future change re-validates there before touching CASE.
consequences: Slower iteration: every meaningful module addition requires a context switch to testaccount. CASE-specific symlinks under ~/dotfiles are preserved as backup files on first activation, not destroyed. testaccount disk usage grows over time as a near-duplicate of CASE's environment. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decisions D1 and D28.

title: Treat live machine state as the authoritative inventory source
context: Three Brewfiles in ~/dotfiles (root Brewfile, personal.brewfile, work.brewfile) all drift substantially from each other and from the live machine. Live brew leaves count is 107 with new tools (gemini-cli, codex, crush, agent-browser, beads/bd) that don't appear in any Brewfile. The historical Brewfiles also carry obviously-stale entries (python@2, mysql@5.6, postgresql@9.6, java8, ethereum tap). Reconciling them is more work than re-deriving from live state.
decision: Inventory is captured from live state: brew leaves + brew list --cask + brew tap + mas list + ls /Applications + ls ~/Library/Fonts + per-domain defaults read + ls of LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon directories. Brewfiles in ~/dotfiles become historical reference only. Each inventory artifact lands under .ai/inventory/ and is re-derived by an independent reviewer agent.
consequences: One-time effort to fan out inventory-capture agents. Some live entries will be intentional drift (sandbox tools); they get added to the ledger anyway per the all-AI-tools-declarative decision. Historical context for why a package was added is lost unless the reviewer agent surfaces it. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D2.

title: Set homebrew.onActivation.cleanup = "none" forever
context: The nix-darwin Homebrew bridge offers cleanup modes none/uninstall/zap. zap forces every brew/cask/MAS app to live in the ledger or be removed at activation. The live machine has 107 leaves, 16 casks, and 141 /Applications entries — some installed manually from .pkg, some experimental AI tools that churn weekly. A strict cleanup mode would create unsafe activations and impose ledger-update toil on every brew install.
decision: homebrew.onActivation.cleanup = "none". Manual brew installs persist alongside the declarative ledger. Drift cleanup, if ever wanted, becomes an explicit human action — never an activation side-effect. Combined with all-AI-tools-declarative this means the ledger is best-effort comprehensive but the bridge never deletes anything the operator didn't ask it to.
consequences: Reproducibility on a fresh Mac depends on ledger completeness; nothing protects against an unrecorded brew install on AVA. Operators must remove unwanted packages manually. The fresh-restore path will not match AVA exactly unless the ledger is updated proactively. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D3.

title: Migrate Nix-packaged CLIs out of Homebrew into Home Manager
context: The live brew leaves list duplicates nixpkgs for dozens of CLIs (bat, fzf, ripgrep, jq, neovim, tmux, btop, htop, gh, lazygit, jj, deno, bun, go, uv, vale, television, tree, hyperfine, sevenzip, fontforge, etc.). Keeping these on Homebrew means the bridge stays large and Home Manager's program modules (programs.gh, programs.tmux, programs.btop, programs.htop, programs.jujutsu, programs.television, programs.direnv) aren't fully leveraged. nixpkgs has all of them at current versions.
decision: All Nix-packaged CLIs move to Home Manager. Tools with first-class programs.* modules get the module form so config is co-located. Bare CLIs land in home.packages. The Homebrew bridge contracts to: GUI casks, Brew-only formulas with no Nix package (gpg-suite, pinentry-mac, mas, mactex, wireshark-app, xquartz, miniconda, ngrok, vagrant, codex, etc.), and MAS apps via masApps.
consequences: Substantial first-pass churn: ~80 leaves get re-homed. Some daemons that brew currently services (mysql, postgresql@14, caddy) need explicit launchd policy from Topic 08. Removing them from brew also unloads their plists — Topic 08 must decide whether to re-declare or retire. Determinate's nix store grows; brew /opt/homebrew shrinks. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decisions D5 and D8.

title: 1Password owns SSH; GPG owns commit and tag signing only
context: Two agents currently exist: 1Password is the SSH agent (~/.ssh/1password-agent.sock, used by zsh, tmux, and git over SSH), and GPG Suite runs gpg-agent for commit signing with key 715CED2327899E28. The Home Manager services.gpg-agent module supports enableSshSupport to make GPG serve SSH too, which would unify but break the current 1Password integration.
decision: Preserve the current split. 1Password remains the only SSH agent. services.gpg-agent.enableSshSupport = false. GPG is configured for signing only — programs.git.signing uses the existing key; pinentry-mac stays for unlock prompts.
consequences: Two agents continue to run side-by-side. Operators must keep 1Password installed and unlocked to do SSH; GPG Suite (pinentry-mac) must stay installed for signing. Future migration to SSH-key-based git signing via ssh-keygen -Y sign would let us drop GPG entirely, but is out of scope. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D10.

title: Vendor all non-system fonts (including paid Operator Mono) in the repo
context: 230 user fonts in ~/Library/Fonts include the paid Operator Mono family with custom Nerd Font Complete patches. The actual on-disk family name is 'Operator Mono * Nerd Font Complete', NOT 'OperatorMono Nerd Font Mono' as older plan text states. Without these specific assets on a fresh Mac, Ghostty and tmux terminals fall back to a generic monospace and break the user's editor experience. The repo is private; vendoring paid font binaries is acceptable.
decision: All non-system fonts get vendored into modules/home-manager/assets/fonts/. The full Operator Mono Nerd Font Complete set is included verbatim. Home Manager installs them into ~/Library/Fonts via home.file or a per-font home.activation step. Ghostty/tmux configs reference the exact 'Operator Mono * Nerd Font Complete' family name.
consequences: Repo size grows by ~50MB of font binaries. Repo must remain private — publishing would distribute paid assets. Fresh-Mac restore reproduces the typography exactly; AVA's existing fonts are left in place (no removal). Adding a new font is a repo commit, not a drag-and-drop. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D11.

title: Inject runtime secrets via 1Password CLI op run + maintain explicit registry
context: Today's secret pattern is ~/dotfiles/shell/op.sh (local, ignored, holds a literal 1Password service-account token) plus scattered .env files (notify.env etc.). Encrypted-in-repo secret stores (sops-nix, agenix) would require an age/gpg key bootstrap chain that conflicts with the 1Password-centric model. 1Password CLI's op run --env-file already serves the runtime injection need with no on-disk plaintext.
decision: Runtime secrets are injected via op run --env-file=<template>. Each consumer script declares its required vars in a tracked template (placeholder values referencing op:// URIs). A registry at .ai/secrets-registry.md tracks every place that needs op but doesn't yet use it — the registry is grown as items are discovered and shrunk as they are migrated. No sops-nix, no agenix.
consequences: Every secret-using process must be wrapped with op run, adding a 1Password unlock dependency at runtime. Non-interactive contexts (launchd jobs, CI) need a service-account token, which itself is a secret that bootstraps the chain. The registry is a living document; out-of-date registry entries hide migration debt. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D12.

title: Zed is the daily editor; nvim and lvim trees survive verbatim via xdg.configFile
context: Live state shows Zed as the actively-used editor: ~/.config/zed/{settings,keymap,tasks}.json are symlinked from ~/dotfiles/zed/, conversation history is in ~/.config/zed/conversations/, and recent mtimes are within days. Neovim and LunarVim trees still exist (with vim-plug + lazy + packer + coc artifacts overlapping) but mtimes suggest occasional use. Translating Neovim into programs.neovim.plugins would be a non-trivial refactor that Topic 03 explicitly defers.
decision: Zed is the primary editor. Settings/keymap/tasks are seeded once via home.activation copy-if-missing — subsequent UI edits stick (no merged baseline). Neovim and LunarVim config trees are carried into modules/home-manager/assets/{nvim,lvim} as curated whitelists and installed via xdg.configFile. No translation to programs.neovim.plugins. LunarVim's runtime install at ~/.local/share/lunarvim and the ~/.local/bin/lvim launcher remain imperative.
consequences: Editor migration is config-only; the underlying runtime stays bootstrapped by vim-plug + LunarVim installer. Future move to programs.neovim is possible without lock-in from this decision. Zed's UI-mutable settings means CASE's customizations diverge from the seed over time; fresh-restore reseeds. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decisions D9 and D13.

title: Preserve ~/dotfiles in place after migration; do not delete or archive
context: ~/dotfiles is the current source of truth (symlinked .tmux.conf, .gitconfig, .vale.ini, ~/.config/nvim, ~/.config/lvim, ~/.config/vale, ~/.config/ghostty/config, .Brewfile, .functions, .scripts, .p10k.zsh, zed JSONs). Once Home Manager owns those paths via hm-backup, the dotfiles symlinks become orphaned. Deleting or moving the directory risks losing history, Operator Mono assets, examples/ references, and git history of every dotfile change over a decade.
decision: After migration, ~/dotfiles stays on disk untouched. Home Manager's hm-backup mechanism renames the symlinked targets to *.hm-backup but the dotfiles directory itself is preserved. No archive step. No content copy from ~/dotfiles into ~/manager — assets are vendored fresh from live files into modules/home-manager/assets/ per the strict whitelist.
consequences: AVA carries permanent dual state: ~/dotfiles plus ~/manager. Operators must remember which is authoritative (~/manager). New developers/agents reading the system will see both and need clear documentation that ~/dotfiles is legacy-historical. Disk usage doubles for the duplicated assets. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decisions D17 and D30.

title: Move SSH private keys into 1Password vault; keep allowed_signers on disk
context: ~/.ssh holds 8 private/public key pairs (id_rsa, gitlab, calhacks_aws, gradebot_rsa, jry.pem, jry-aws-temp.pem, infinite-music, tdna, zigguratum). Many are stale (gitlab 2016, calhacks_aws 2016, gradebot_rsa 2017, jry-aws-temp 2021). 1Password already serves the agent (~/.ssh/1password-agent.sock). Per-host IdentityFile entries can be replaced with IdentityAgent pointing at the 1Password socket, eliminating on-disk private keys entirely.
decision: Every private key migrates into the 1Password vault. On-disk private keys are deleted from ~/.ssh once the 1Password vault entry is confirmed working. ~/.ssh/config matchBlocks use IdentityAgent (pointing at the 1Password socket) instead of IdentityFile. The only files that stay on disk are: ~/.ssh/config (managed by programs.ssh), ~/.ssh/allowed_signers (managed by home.file), and the 1password-agent.sock symlink. known_hosts and known_hosts.old remain user-managed but unmanaged by Nix.
consequences: Operators must unlock 1Password to use SSH (already true). Recovery from 1Password lockout becomes critical — losing the vault means losing every SSH identity. Migrating each key is a one-time manual step per host (audit which keys are still in use, paste private + public into a vault entry, update config). Stale keys get retired in the process rather than carried forward. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D18.

title: Use /adr for fine-grained decisions; DECISIONS.md for tranche summaries
context: The repo already requires DECISIONS.md updates per CLAUDE.md at the end of every session. The /adr skill provides a structured JSONL log with monotonic IDs and supersede semantics — better for individual architectural choices that may be revisited. Mixing both gives queryable detail (adr.jsonl) plus narrative continuity (DECISIONS.md).
decision: DECISIONS.md continues to be appended at session boundaries with tranche-level summaries (what shipped, what surprised). adr.jsonl records each non-trivial architectural decision as its own ADR via the adr CLI. Decisions can be superseded with --supersedes when they are revisited. The two layers are complementary: DECISIONS.md is human-narrative, adr.jsonl is machine-queryable.
consequences: Operators need to know both stores exist. ADR IDs become a stable reference target in plan documents and commit messages. Risk of duplicate recording — same decision in both places — is acceptable because each serves a different audience. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D24.

title: Keep gitego for path-based identity; generate its config declaratively
context: ~/.gitego/config.yaml defines 5 identities (jry, inf, tdna, zigg, keybase) with per-path auto_rules. The repo's ~/dotfiles/git/gitconfig already references gitego credential helper and uses [includeIf] hooks pointing at ~/.gitego/profiles/*.gitconfig. Replacing gitego with native git includeIf rules is possible but loses the credential-helper integration that handles SSH key selection per identity.
decision: gitego stays. Home Manager generates ~/.gitego/config.yaml from a Nix attrset (modules/home-manager/git.nix), so identities, ssh_keys, and auto_rules are version-controlled. The per-profile gitconfig fragments under ~/.gitego/profiles/ are also generated. programs.git enables the gitego credential helper and the includeIf rules. gitego itself is installed via go install / brew.
consequences: Adding/removing an identity is a Nix attribute edit and a switch. SSH key paths in gitego config will need to align with the SSH-keys-to-1Password decision (ADR 10) — likely meaning gitego entries reference IdentityAgent socket + key fingerprint rather than file paths. gitego's upstream support matters; if it goes unmaintained, this decision must be revisited. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D25.

title: Defer Touch ID sudo and firewall enable; keep current security posture
context: Topics 09 (networking/firewall) and 12 (/etc/PAM, sudo, Touch ID) would change current behavior: firewall is off (Little Snitch handles outbound), Touch ID sudo isn't configured, /etc/pam.d/sudo_local.template exists but isn't activated. Enabling either is a behavior change that could surprise existing tooling (vagrant networking, headless launchd jobs, etc.) and isn't required for the deterministic-reproduction goal.
decision: Topic 09 and Topic 12 are explicitly out of scope for this migration. /etc/hosts is the one exception (per separate decision D26) because the current facebook block list is intentional state worth preserving. PAM sudo, firewall, sudoers, and security.pam.services.* are not modified. The current security posture is encoded as-is by declaring no changes.
consequences: Fresh-Mac restore will have Touch ID sudo off and firewall off, matching AVA. Re-enabling either later is a single Nix attribute change but requires re-testing every workflow that touches sudo or network egress. Decision can be revisited after Tranche D lands. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D27.

title: testaccount is the permanent validation seat, not a one-shot user
context: Once CASE is migrated, the easy path is to delete testaccount to reclaim disk and reduce account count. But the migration introduces a long stream of future changes (Tranches B–E + ongoing tweaks), and every one of those benefits from being tested first on a clean account before touching CASE.
decision: testaccount persists indefinitely. Every meaningful future change to flake.nix or modules/* runs first as a darwin-rebuild switch under testaccount with smoke tests, then under CASE only after passing. This is the same flow used during initial migration. testaccount remains a /bin/zsh login user with a separate ~/Library state so its activations don't write into CASE's home directory.
consequences: Permanent disk overhead for testaccount's home directory and any home-manager outputs in /nix/store referenced only by testaccount. Switching to testaccount for validation slows iteration. Net win: regressions caught on testaccount can't strand CASE's daily-driver session. See .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md decision D28.

title: MIGRATION.md supersedes older topic memos and stale epic bodies on conflict
context: manager-4.4, 4.5, 4.6 (and the rest of 4.7-4.10) were drafted before the May 2026 interview. Their description text and the topic memos they reference (.ai/plan/01-packages-applications.md, .ai/plan/15-homebrew-itself.md, etc.) carry assumptions that D2/D3/D5/D8 explicitly retire: live state is now authoritative inventory (D2), brew cleanup stays "none" forever (D3), Nix-packaged CLIs aggressively move into Home Manager (D5), AI tools are all declarative (D8). Rewriting every epic body in beads to match would burn session time we'd rather spend on inventory and Tranche A implementation; leaving them stale would let implementers pick contradictory directions.
decision: Treat .ai/plan/MIGRATION.md (D1-D31) plus this adr.jsonl as the single authoritative implementation contract. When an older topic memo or an existing manager-4.* epic body conflicts with MIGRATION.md or an ADR, MIGRATION.md/ADR wins. Implementers reconcile the topic memo and the ticket body in the same PR that lands the conflicting change, recording the supersede in that ticket's notes and a session DECISIONS.md entry. No mass rewrite of existing tickets up front.
consequences: Anyone reading the older 4.4-4.10 epic bodies must cross-check MIGRATION.md before implementing; reading order is MIGRATION.md, ADRs, then topic memo as supplemental. Drift between epic body and MIGRATION.md will linger until the implementing PR cleans it up. Operator must remember the dual-source rule (covered by ADR 11 + this ADR). If MIGRATION.md is itself later revised, the new revision lands as a fresh ADR that supersedes this one rather than as ad-hoc edits to MIGRATION.md.

title: Pre-clear dotfile symlinks before HM activation
context: First darwin-rebuild switch under testaccount failed at HM linkGeneration on /Users/CASE/.zshrc, /Users/CASE/.zprofile, and /Users/CASE/.config/ghostty/config. The files were symlinks pointing into ~/dotfiles (per D17 untouched). home-manager.backupFileExtension = "hm-backup" (D25) silently does not apply to symlinks — only regular files with non-matching content. linkGeneration aborted the whole user activation and rolled back, leaving no HM state for CASE. Activation only succeeded after the three symlinks were rm'd by hand. Fresh-Mac restores will trip on the same trap whenever the new operator's home already contains symlinks at HM-owned target paths.
decision: Document pre-clearance as part of the supported install path. Before running darwin-rebuild switch on a host that has a pre-existing dotfile layout (typical for any non-virgin macOS account), the operator removes every symlink at an HM-managed target path. Where this can be scripted in ./install, add an idempotent symlink-only sweep that targets HM-owned paths (.zshrc, .zprofile, .zshenv, .config/ghostty/config, .config/jj/config.toml, .config/television/config.toml, .config/gh/config.yml, .config/gh-dash/config.yml, .config/btop/btop.conf, .config/htop, .ssh/config, .gnupg/{gpg,gpg-agent}.conf, .gitego/config.yaml, .vale.ini, .gitignore, .p10k.zsh, plus Library/Fonts/* and the editor seed trees). Remove only entries that are symlinks AND whose target lies under $HOME/dotfiles (or any explicitly listed legacy root); never regular files. Real files keep the existing backupFileExtension path.
consequences: Adds one new install-time step that is mandatory on hosts with pre-existing dotfile symlinks but a no-op on virgin Macs. Risk surface narrows: deleting a symlink whose target lives in ~/dotfiles leaves that target intact (D17), so the operator can rebuild the old layout if anything goes wrong. The alternative — letting HM error out at linkGeneration — is worse because it rolls back the entire user-level activation and leaves the system in a half-applied state (system profile changed, HM did not run). Implementation lives outside this ADR; track via a manager-* ticket. Until that lands, the operator handles the sweep manually and records it in DECISIONS.md per session.

title: Build gitego YAML with explicit lines, not Nix multiline strings
context: modules/home-manager/git.nix initially rendered ~/.gitego/config.yaml using nested Nix '\'\'...''\'' multiline strings. The optional ssh_key line was emitted from a separate '\'\'...''\'' block whose minimum indent included the leading blank line, so Nix's indent-stripping left ssh_key at column 0 instead of inside its profile. Profile keys (inf:, jry:, ...) also ended up unindented because the outer interpolation point was already at column 0 after stripping. Result: a structurally broken file where 'ssh_key' appeared as a duplicate top-level mapping key. gitego list refused to load the file with 'mapping key "ssh_key" already defined'. The smoke harness did not catch this because no check exercised the gitego binary.
decision: Render gitego config.yaml from an explicit list of lines joined with newline, not from nested '\'\'...''\'' strings. The renderIdentity and renderAutoRule helpers build [ "  key:" "    field: value" ... ] and lib.concatStringsSep '\n' the result. The outer gitegoConfigYaml then interpolates those flat-line blobs. Add a smoke-harness check that runs 'gitego list' against the generated file so a future renderer regression is caught the next time testaccount validates a switch.
consequences: The renderer is verbose vs the original multiline form, but the output is now provably correct: a fresh darwin-rebuild switch produced a config.yaml that gitego list accepts and that reports the five expected identities (inf, jry, keybase, tdna, zigg) with jry active. Future identity additions extend the renderIdentity line list rather than threading more multiline blocks. Same lesson applies to any other config.yaml/.yml/.toml/.json we generate from Nix: avoid nested '\'\'...''\'' when the document has optional fields, and back the generation with a smoke check that parses the artifact end-to-end.

title: Manage /etc/hosts blocklist via system.activationScripts
context: D26 specified 'declare the /etc/hosts facebook block list via networking.hosts'. Inspection of nix-darwin 25.11 source (/nix/store/.../nix-darwin/modules/networking/default.nix) confirms the module exposes only computerName/hostName/localHostName/domain/knownNetworkServices/dns/search/wakeOnLan.enable. There is no networking.hosts, no networking.extraHosts, and no networking.hostFiles option. The activation script only handles a restore-from-backup path on uninstall. D26's prescribed mechanism does not exist on the target platform.
decision: Land /etc/hosts management in modules/darwin/hosts.nix using system.activationScripts. The script writes a single delimited managed block (BEGIN/END markers) into /etc/hosts containing every 0.0.0.0 entry from .ai/inventory/etc-hosts-blocks.txt. Re-runs strip the existing managed block and emit a fresh one — idempotent by construction. The pre-Nix /etc/hosts is snapshotted to /etc/hosts.before-managed-block on first run so the operator can recover the original. Apple-default header (localhost, broadcasthost, ::1) stays in place — nothing outside the managed block is touched.
consequences: D26's letter (use networking.hosts) is superseded; D26's intent (declarative facebook + tracker blocklist preserved across rebuilds) is satisfied. Updating the blocklist now means editing .ai/inventory/etc-hosts-blocks.txt and rebuilding. The activation script is root-only (runs inside sudo darwin-rebuild) and modifies /etc/hosts in place, which is the standard nix-darwin pattern for files macOS expects to live at fixed paths. Adding /etc/hosts entries is now a code change with full git history, not an ad-hoc sudo edit.
